guidelines.detail: same as LRN-014 (The description explicitly assigns the cited activities to roles, while the generated labels omit those performers. This guideline matches learned guideline LRN-014; it also aligns with documented guideline ACT-06, which says to model stated responsibility and prefer lanes for ordinary organizational responsibility. P1 is not relevant to this guideline.)

same as LRN-006 (The description states that preparations happen while the waiter readies the cart, and that delivery begins once the food, wine, and cart are ready. This supports concurrent branches followed by synchronization; LRN-006 already expresses essentially the same guideline.)

same as LRN-035 (The description explicitly assigns activities to roles, while several generated task labels omit those stated responsibilities. LRN-035 already expresses this guideline, so it is not a new rule.)

same as LRN-005 (The cited missing flows show that stated progressions and transitions through a synchronization point were not connected. This is consistent with the description and BPMN semantics, and LRN-005 already expresses essentially the same guideline.)

same as LRN-014 (The description assigns several activities to named roles, while the generated task labels omit those actors compared with the reference labels. The proposed guideline is already captured by learned guideline LRN-014. I did not rely on P1 because the description does not establish a meaningful outcome label for the end event.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names multiple required activities without specifying their order and states that a later outcome depends on all of them: Model the activities as parallel branches and synchronize them before that outcome.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a shared activity is followed by work assigned to multiple roles that can proceed concurrently, and a later outcome depends on all of that work

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description explicitly identifies a role or participant as responsible for performing an activity: Represent that responsibility in the corresponding activity label or in the responsible lane; do not leave the responsibility unrepresented when the description states it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description explicitly identifies the role or participant responsible for an activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description identifies a role or group as responsible for performing an activity: Label the corresponding BPMN activity so that the stated responsibility remains clear, without adding unstated details.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description assigns an activity to a specific role or participant

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents distinct activities in an ordered progression, including transitions into, through, or out of branches or synchronization points: Connect each consecutive activity with a sequence flow, preserving the stated transitions through branches and synchronization points.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an order or dependency between distinct activities or gateways, including transitions into or out of branches or synchronization points.
